STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or any image prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently and establish:

Verified core facts — what actually happened, who was involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, and popular myth.

The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.

The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.

Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume, light, scale).

Uncertainties — anything sources disagree on or you cannot verify. NEVER invent quotations, Sanskrit verses, dates, statistics, dialogue from scripture, or miracles presented as scientific proof. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYA
MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 7.3 IMAGE-ONLY
Bible + Script Prompt + Image-Only Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, in one document — Static Visual Edition
This single file merges the original documents into one complete IMAGE-ONLY visual production system with Studio Motion Graphics.

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL (Narration + Visuals + Motion Graphics / Metadata)
This pipeline enforces a strict THREE-TAG SYSTEM:

1. Audio Narration Tag: Exactly one <script>...</script> block housing the clean TTS-ready narration in Section 2B. Spoken Devanagari Hindi only.

2. Dynamic Numbered Image Tags: Sequential <image_prompt0>, <image_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, ... <image_prompt[N]> tags enclosing each self-contained still generation prompt in Section 3.
- Crucial Rule on <image_prompt0>: Index 0 is strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail (16:9). It is never placed inside the video editing timeline.
- Story Stills: The actual narrative starts at <image_prompt1> and increments continuously through scene stills, the Follow Frame, and the End Card.

3. Dynamic Motion Graphics & Metadata Tags: Sequential <metadata1>, <metadata2>, ... <metadata[N]> tags specifying high-retention studio motion graphics (scripture scrolls, era timelines, sacred maps, relic reticles, canto titles).
The AI decides where and when to trigger each motion graphic based on the sacred story beats, but MUST include them where relevant:

Available Motion Graphic Archetypes for <metadata>:
- scripture_scroll: Use for sacred Sanskrit shlokas, ancient verses, or prophetic decrees with Hindi meaning/translation. Displays authentic aged parchment/copper-plate card with golden callout.
  Format:
  <metadata1>
  #scene 2
  Type: scripture_scroll
  Title: [Sanskrit Shloka / Key Mantra]
  Detail: [Source e.g. VALMIKI RAMAYANA // BALA KANDA or Translation]
  </metadata1>

- telemetry_counter: Use whenever explicit numbers, years of exile/penance, elapsed centuries, arrow counts, or astronomical alignments are spoken. Displays rapid odometer ticker count up (0 -> target).
  Format:
  <metadata2>
  #scene 4
  Type: telemetry_counter
  Target: [Integer numeral e.g. 14]
  Unit: [YEARS / BCE / YUGA / ARROWS]
  Label: [ERA / PENANCE / DURATION]
  Detail: [Context e.g. 14 Years of Forest Exile]
  </metadata2>

- route_map: Use for epic journeys, exile paths, flight routes (Pushpaka Vimana), or sacred trails (Ayodhya -> Dandaka -> Kishkindha -> Lanka). Displays animated vector route line drawing with radar destination ping.
  Format:
  <metadata3>
  #scene 6
  Type: route_map
  Origin: [Starting location e.g. Ayodhya]
  Destination: [Arrival place e.g. Panchavati]
  Distance: [Route descriptor e.g. DANDAKARANYA TRAIL]
  Detail: [Sacred Exile Journey]
  </metadata3>

- relic_spotlight: Use to direct viewer focus to a sacred divine weapon (Sharanga Bow, Brahmastra), holy relic (Chudamani, Rama's signet ring), or temple architecture visible in the scene. Displays pulsing targeting reticle and callout line.
  Format:
  <metadata4>
  #scene 8
  Type: object_spotlight
  Target: [Sacred item visible in scene e.g. Kodanda Bow / Sanjeevani Herb]
  Title: [Name of Sacred Relic / Astra]
  Detail: [Divine power / Origin / Significance]
  </metadata4>

- polaroid_badge: Use when introducing a legendary sage, king, avatar, or warrior (e.g. Maharishi Vishwamitra, Jatayu, Meghanada). Displays card cutout with 3D tilt and drifting motion over the scene. Must include an Asset Prompt for an isolated subject on clean background.
  Format:
  <metadata5>
  #scene 3
  Type: polaroid_badge
  Title: [Character Name e.g. MAHARISHI VISHWAMITRA]
  Detail: [Lineage / Title / Role e.g. Brahmarshi / Preceptor]
  Asset Prompt: [Self-contained visual prompt for isolated subject on clean background]
  </metadata5>

- chapter_title: Use for major canto openings, act breaks, or epic turning points. Bold cinematic typography with accent tag.
  Format:
  <metadata6>
  #scene 1
  Type: chapter_title
  Title: [Canto / Chapter Headline e.g. THE LEAP TO LANKA]
  Tag: [BALA KANDA / ARANYA KANDA / SUNDARA KANDA]
  </metadata6>

All AI video, motion prompts, and animation directions are completely removed. Every visual asset is a detailed, static prompt.

Midpoint Re-Hook: At 50–60% mark, introduce a 5–8 word revelation or sudden reversal.

Ending: Story reaches completion first; followed by ONE single 3-second closing blessing line.

# Research Dossier: The Lost Sarasvati River — Sacred Vedic Geography and Satellite Palaeochannel Evidence

**Target Video Duration:** ~90 Seconds  
**Narration Language:** Hindi (Devanagari script)  
**Core Emotion:** Awe & Scientific Discovery  
**Single Payoff:** Satellite radar evidence (ISRO/NASA) revealing the dried Ghaggar-Hakra subterranean palaeochannel beneath the Thar Desert, confirming that ancient Vedic geographical descriptions reflect real prehistoric river hydraulics rather than pure myth.

---

## 1. Verified Facts, Background & Key Data

### A. Vedic Canon & Geographical Texts
* **Rigvedic Titles:** In Rigveda (Mandala 2, Sukta 41, Verse 16), the Sarasvati is venerated with the superlatives: *"Ambitame Naditame Devitame Sarasvati"* ("Best of Mothers, Best of Rivers, Best of Goddesses").
* **Physical Trajectory in Text:** Rigveda 7.95.2 describes her course as *"Giribhya a samudrat"* ("Flowing pure and unbroken from the mountains to the ocean/sea").
* **Hydraulic Character:** Depicted as a roaring, mighty, glacier-fed river (*saptathi sindhumata* - having seven tributaries/sisters) breaking down mountain precipices with impetuous waves.

### B. Satellite Palaeochannel & Remote Sensing Evidence
* **Palaeochannel Definition:** A palaeochannel is a remnant of an inactive river or stream channel that has been filled or buried by younger sedimentary deposits.
* **Key Space Agencies & Studies:** Remote sensing studies conducted by **ISRO (Regional Remote Sensing Service Centre - RRSSC, Jodhpur & SAC Ahmedabad)**, using **IRS-1C/1D, Landsat, WiFS, LISS-III, and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR / Sentinel-1A)**.
* **Radar Penetration Mechanism:** Microwave radar signals penetrate dry surface sand dunes in arid zones, detecting subterranean moisture anomalies, fine alluvial silt, and dense clay beds hidden 2 to 10 meters beneath the Thar Desert surface.
* **Mapped Course:** Satellite mapping traces a continuous, subterranean channel system 6 to 12 km wide running from the Shivalik foothills through Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab, northern Rajasthan (Anupgarh, Tanot, Jaisalmer), down into the Cholistan Desert (Pakistan) and terminating near the Rann of Kutch.

### C. Geological Desiccation & Archaeological Correlation
* **Ghaggar-Hakra Link:** The present-day seasonal monsoon stream *Ghaggar* (India) and dried bed *Hakra* (Pakistan) occupy the exact path of the satellite-delineated ancient Sarasvati palaeochannel.
* **Tectonic & Climatic Causes of Disappearance:**
  1. *Tectonic Divergence:* Himalayan uplift and seismic events (circa 2500–1900 BCE) caused river avulsion, diverting the **palaeo-Sutlej** west into the Indus system and the **palaeo-Yamuna** east into the Ganga system.
  2. *Monsoon Weakening:* The 4.2k BP climatic event reduced glacial melt and monsoon rainfall, turning a perennial glacier-fed river into a seasonal stream, leading to its eventual desiccation by ~1900 BCE.
* **Harappan Settlement Density:** Over 60% of major Indus-Sarasvati urban archaeological sites (e.g., **Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi, Banawali, Bhirrana**) are clustered directly along the Ghaggar-Hakra palaeochannel bed rather than the main Indus River.

---

## 2. Chronological Story Arc & Scene Beats (~90s Target)

```
00:00 ------------------- 00:12 ------------------- 00:32 ------------------- 00:55 ------------------- 01:15 ------------------- 01:30
|-- Beat 1: Hook Question --|-- Beat 2: Vedic Geography --|-- Beat 3: Satellite Radar --|-- Beat 4: Geological Cause --|-- Beat 5: Payoff & Heritage --|
```

### Beat 1: The Intriguing Hook (00:00 – 00:12)
* **Narrative Focus:** Opening core question — Myth vs. Geological Truth.
* **Content:** Introduce the legend of the vanished Sarasvati River. Contrast ancient oral memory with the modern arid landscape of the Thar Desert.
* **Visual Action:** High-altitude satellite view of the arid Thar Desert morphing seamlessly into a glowing, lush, prehistoric river basin.

### Beat 2: Sacred Vedic Geography & Rigvedic Hymns (00:12 – 00:32)
* **Narrative Focus:** Authentic scripture descriptions of *Naditama*.
* **Content:** Cite Rigveda (2.41.16: *Ambitame Naditame Devitame*) and 7.95.2 (*Giribhya a samudrat*). Establish that ancient seers described a massive, glacier-fed perennial river flowing from the Himalayas to the ocean.
* **Visual Action:** Cinematic dawn shot of an ancient Vedic riverbank (~3000 BCE). Saffron oil lamps on stone altars, majestic flowing turquoise waters, Rishis chanting.

### Beat 3: Space Technology & Satellite Palaeochannel Reveal (00:32 – 00:55)
* **Narrative Focus:** How ISRO remote sensing radar sees beneath desert sands.
* **Content:** Explain the science of palaeochannel mapping. Microwave Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) cuts through Thar Desert sand dunes to uncover buried riverbed paths 6–12 km wide.
* **Visual Action:** Modern Earth-observation satellite in orbit emitting radar sensor grids. Below, thermal satellite imagery reveals glowing cyan subterranean river channels running beneath golden desert dunes.

### Beat 4: Tectonic Shift, Ghaggar-Hakra & Harappan Civilizations (00:55 – 01:15)
* **Narrative Focus:** The physical reality of the Ghaggar-Hakra bed and river avulsion.
* **Content:** Explain how tectonic shifts diverted the palaeo-Sutlej and palaeo-Yamuna rivers away, causing Sarasvati's desiccation around 1900 BCE. Mention Harappan settlements (Rakhigarhi, Kalibangan) thriving on her banks.
* **Visual Action:** Animated split map overlaying Harappan archaeological ruins (Kalibangan/Rakhigarhi) directly along the subterranean Ghaggar-Hakra satellite path.

### Beat 5: Earned Payoff & Heritage Insight (01:15 – 01:30)
* **Narrative Focus:** Scientific validation of cultural memory and preserving subterranean heritage.
* **Content:** Resolve the title promise: Modern space science proves Vedic hymns captured genuine environmental history. Highlight that these buried channels still hold massive subterranean groundwater reserves today.
* **Visual Action:** Seamless transition from space radar telemetry back to a serene modern desert landscape at golden hour, where subterranean blue light pulses under the sand, symbolizing living heritage.

## 3. Visual & World-Building Canon

### A. Environment & Lighting Palette
* **Vedic Era (Pre-2000 BCE):** Soft, warm saffron and gold sunrise light through atmospheric river mist. Deep emerald greenery along riverbanks, crystal-clear glacial blue water, terracotta clay altars (*Yajna Kunds*) with warm flame flickering.
* **Modern Space Sensing Era:** Deep cosmic black space background with vibrant blue Earth curve. High-tech GIS vector overlays: high-contrast thermal satellite imagery using cyan/electric-blue false color for subterranean moisture against warm ochre sand dunes.

* **Harappan Architecture:** Burnt-brick urban structures, wide planned streets, and defensive walls of Kalibangan/Rakhigarhi set against dry river terraces.
* **Topography:** Transition from Shivalik mountain foothills to the flat alluvial plains of Haryana/Rajasthan and the expansive dunes of the Thar Desert.
